record.original_question: In the q-coloring model on bounded-degree graphs, what is the sharp threshold in q versus Delta separating guaranteed uniqueness from possible nonuniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures? In particular, is the classical q>2Delta condition sharp, or can the true borderline be as low as q>Delta (as suggested by tree behavior)?

evidence.quote: It is natural to ask whether the borderline 2Delta is sharp ... Even for the Delta-regular tree, the correct borderline is not known ... For trees the Gibbs measure may well be unique as soon as q > Delta; and it is at least conceivable that this is the sharp borderline for general graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a (possibly infinite) graph of maximum degree Δ, and fix an integer q ≥ 2. A proper q-coloring of G is a map σ: V(G) → {1,…,q} with σ(u) ≠ σ(v) for every edge {u,v}. For a finite subgraph, the uniform proper q-coloring measure assigns equal probability to all proper q-colorings; for infinite G, an infinite-volume Gibbs measure is a probability measure on {1,…,q}^{V(G)} whose conditional distribution on any finite set W, given the configuration on V(G) ∖ W, is uniform on the proper q-colorings of W extending the boundary condition (the DLR equations).

It is classical that if q > 2Δ then, for every graph of maximum degree at most Δ, there is a unique infinite-volume Gibbs measure for proper q-colorings. On the infinite Δ-regular tree T_Δ, non-uniqueness can occur when q ≤ Δ+1 (boundary conditions can rigidify the root).

Determine the sharp threshold function q*(Δ) — the smallest q such that every graph of maximum degree at most Δ admits a unique infinite-volume Gibbs measure of proper q-colorings whenever q ≥ q*(Δ). In particular:

(a) Is the bound q > 2Δ sharp for general bounded-degree graphs, or can it be improved?

(b) Already on the Δ-regular tree T_Δ, determine the precise threshold: is the Gibbs measure for uniform proper q-colorings of T_Δ unique for all q ≥ Δ+1 (i.e., is "q > Δ" the sharp tree threshold)?

(c) Is the sharp tree threshold also the sharp threshold for the class of all graphs of maximum degree at most Δ?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress is known but the sharp threshold is not settled. Jonasson proved uniqueness on the Δ-regular tree for q ≥ Δ+2; for q ≤ Δ+1 frozen boundary conditions can give non-uniqueness on the tree, but the precise tree threshold (around q = Δ+1) is not fully resolved in general. For general bounded-degree graphs, the classical q > 2Δ uniqueness bound has been improved by various authors (e.g., Vigoda's q > (11/6)Δ regime in related contexts and subsequent work), but determining whether the true threshold matches the tree threshold remains open. Recent work (e.g., on anti-ferromagnetic Potts uniqueness on Δ-regular trees for large Δ) provides progress but not a full sharp threshold.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness thresholds on trees versus graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the relation between uniqueness of Gibbs measure on Δ-regular trees and on general bounded-degree graphs for colorings and related models.
status_evidence.claim: The precise relation between tree thresholds and graph thresholds for colorings is studied but not fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of the Gibbs measure for the anti-ferromagnetic Potts model on the infinite Δ-regular tree for large Δ
status_evidence.snippet: For q ≥ 5 and Δ sufficiently large, uniqueness holds on the Δ-regular tree above a threshold w_c; this is recent progress (2022–2023).
status_evidence.claim: Sharp tree thresholds for related Potts/coloring models have only been partially established.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of the Gibbs measure for the 4-state anti-ferromagnetic Potts model on the regular tree
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes uniqueness for 4-coloring/Potts case on the regular tree under specific conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Even on the regular tree, results are obtained case by case, and the q vs Δ borderline is not fully known.
